subject: math

objective.text: Solve word problems using data presented in a bar graph.

explanations.title: Money in a graph
explanations.text: A bar graph can show money, like the number of dimes or nickels each child has. Read the bar to find each number.

explanations.title: Start the scale at 0
explanations.text: The scale starts at 0, not 1. A ruler helps you remember.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (the beginning of the scale is 0 and not 1)

explanations.title: Find the total
explanations.text: To find the total, add all the numbers in the graph.

source_ref.section: Student Debrief (find the total amount of coins recorded)

explanations.title: Doubling
explanations.text: If a number doubles, add it to itself. To show a bigger number, add more boxes or let each box stand for 2.

explanations.title: Compare with a smaller unknown
explanations.text: 'More' can make you add, but sometimes you subtract. Draw a tape diagram to see which. Rita has 27 pennies, 19 more than Carlos. Carlos has fewer, so subtract.

examples.title: Rita and Carlos
examples.text: Rita has 27 pennies. That is 19 more than Carlos. 27 minus 19 equals 8. Carlos has 8 pennies.

examples.title: Callista's pennies
examples.text: Saturday 15, Sunday 10, Monday 4 and Tuesday 7. In all, 15 plus 10 plus 4 plus 7 equals 36 pennies.

questions.text: I am holding up a coin worth 25 cents. What is the name of the coin?
How much is a quarter worth?
A quarter and a nickel are in the can. How many cents are in the can?
A quarter and a dime are in the can. How many cents are in the can?
Rita has 19 more pennies than Carlos. Rita has 27 pennies. How many pennies does Carlos have?
What number does the count scale start at? Use a ruler to help you.
Emily has 8 dimes. If you doubled her dimes, how many dimes would she have?
How could you show 16 dimes on a graph that has fewer boxes?
How did you find the total amount of coins in the graph? Share your strategy.
Think of a question to ask your class that you could turn into a bar graph. What is the title and what are the categories?
Callista saved pennies: Saturday 15, Sunday 10, Monday 4 and Tuesday 7. How many pennies did she save in all?
Her sister saved 18 fewer pennies. How many pennies did her sister save?
How much more money did Callista save on Saturday than on Monday and Tuesday?
Callista doubles the amount she saved on Sunday. How many pennies is that for Sunday?
Friends counted nickels: Annie 5, Scarlett 11, Remy 8 and LaShay 14. How many nickels do the children have in all?
What is the total value of Annie's and Remy's coins, in cents?
How many fewer nickels does Remy have than LaShay?
Who has less money, Annie and Scarlett, or Remy and LaShay?
Dimes: Emily 8, Andrew 12, Thomas 6 and Ava 13. How many more dimes does Andrew have than Emily?
How many fewer dimes does Thomas have than Ava and Emily?
Which pair has more dimes, Emily and Ava, or Andrew and Thomas? How many more?
What is the total number of dimes if all four children put their dimes together?
Dimes donated: Madison 12, Robin 10, Benjamin 15 and Miguel 13. How many more dimes did Miguel donate than Robin?
How many fewer dimes did Madison donate than Robin and Benjamin?
How many more dimes does Miguel need to donate the same as Benjamin and Madison?
How many dimes were donated in all?
Dimes: Lacy 6, Sam 11, Stefanie 9 and Amber 14. How many more dimes does Amber have than Stefanie?
How many more dimes do Sam and Lacy need to save to equal Stefanie and Amber?
Nickels: Justin 13, Melissa 9, Meghan 12 and Douglas 7. How many more nickels does Meghan have than Melissa?
How many fewer nickels does Douglas have than Justin?
Which pair has more nickels, Justin and Melissa, or Douglas and Meghan? How many more?
What is the total number of nickels if all four children put theirs together?
Dimes donated: Kylie 12, Tom 10, John 15 and Shannon 13. How many dimes did Shannon donate?
How many fewer dimes did Kylie donate than John and Shannon?
How many more dimes does Tom need to donate the same as Shannon and Kylie?
How many dimes were donated in all?
